chief_complaint: Chronic musculoskeletal pain (low back pain and knee osteoarthritis) managed with opioid and NSAID therapy, complicated by substance misuse and multiple metabolic risk factors.
history_of_present_illness: The patient has endured chronic low back pain and knee osteoarthritis since 2012-2014, for which she receives hydrocodone/acetaminophen and naproxen. Over the past several years she has developed a pattern of drug misuse (onset 2019) and is currently prescribed an opioid, raising concern for opioid use disorder. She reports ongoing intimate‑partner abuse since 2020, contributing to psychosocial stress. Obesity (BMI ≥30) has been present since the mid‑1990s and is associated with prediabetes (A1c 6.9%) and stage‑1 hypertension (131/85 mmHg). Anemia has been documented since 1992, and chronic sinusitis has been a persistent issue. Dental disease (loss of teeth, prior gingivitis) remains untreated. She is employed full‑time and has higher education, but her risk‑activity involvement and substance use suggest additional behavioral health needs. Preventive care appears limited: no antihypertensive, lipid‑lowering, or glucose‑lowering agents are prescribed, and key labs (eGFR, cholesterol) are missing.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior fever, chills, cough, sputum production, and a COVID‑19 infection in early 2021. The patient had two concussions in late 2020 that resolved. Dental health issues such as gingivitis and gingival disease were treated in 2020. A miscarriage occurred in 1999. No other chronic resolved diagnoses are recorded.

risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk: stage‑1 hypertension (131/85 mmHg), obesity (BMI ≥30), prediabetes (A1c 6.9%). Metabolic risk: elevated BMI, prediabetes, likely dyslipidemia (lipid panel missing). Renal risk: chronic NSAID use with no eGFR data. Hematologic risk: chronic anemia of unknown etiology. Musculoskeletal risk: chronic low back pain, knee osteoarthritis, chronic NSAID exposure. Psychiatric/behavioral risk: documented drug misuse, intimate‑partner abuse, possible sleep disturbance (diphenhydramine). Dental risk: loss of teeth, prior gingivitis. Comorbidity flags confirm anemia and osteoarthritis. Charlson index 1, clinical complexity moderate.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with high‑impact chronic musculoskeletal pain managed with opioid and NSAID therapy, active drug misuse, obesity, prediabetes, stage‑1 hypertension, anemia, and ongoing intimate‑partner violence. These factors place her at elevated risk for opioid use disorder, cardiovascular disease, renal injury from NSAIDs, and psychosocial instability. Comprehensive care should address pain management, substance use treatment, cardiovascular risk reduction, mental health support, and safety planning.
